analysis: Market context: Broad indices in mixed-to-recovering state after tariff-shock volatility; many quality names have re-rated down 20-40% from 52w highs, creating Stage 1 basing setups in the lower half of their ranges. The portfolio is essentially all-cash ($100k) with a trivial NNDM stub that can be ignored for sizing. Opportunity: deploy ~55-60% into 3 high-conviction, value-quality setups while keeping ~40% in cash as a cushion for further entries or volatility. Candidates selected for: (1) superior fundamental quality at deeply discounted valuations, (2) technical basing with either confirmed uptrend or SMA50 beginning to turn, (3) asymmetric risk/reward with ATR-based stops. PYPL leads on value/momentum combo (fwd P/E 8.71, basing uptrend, FCF yield >7%). ADBE offers exceptional quality at a generational valuation discount (fwd P/E 9.5, PEG 0.70, ROE 59%). APP represents a structurally dominant ad-tech platform with extraordinary margins compounding at 66% revenue growth. All three are sized so maximum loss per position is ~1.35-1.5% of portfolio equity. Total heat if all three stop out simultaneously: ~4.3%, well within acceptable drawdown limits. Confidence in ~1% weekly compounding is moderate given we are early in a base-building phase — trend confirmation is still developing.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit buy at $50.00-$50.50 on any intraday dip toward current price; acceptable to enter at market open. Avoid chasing if price gaps above $52 without consolidation.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: PayPal is priced for secular decline but the business generates $3.3B FCF annually on a $45B market cap (>7% FCF yield). Fwd P/E of 8.71 and PEG of 0.91 imply the market expects zero growth — a deeply undemanding bar for a network-effect payments platform with 25.7% ROE. Operating margins expanding and Venmo/Braintree monetization still early. Alex Chriss restructuring is showing early traction. Technical: Confirmed uptrend with SMA50 slope +2.3% over 20 days. Price 8% above SMA50 but only at 30% of 52w range — not extended. Base forming above prior breakdown zone around $44-46. Uptrend basing is precisely the Stage 1→2 transition the strategy targets.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if price closes 2 consecutive days below SMA50 (thesis break). Time stop: reassess in 90 days if target not approached. Take partial profits at $60 (first resistance). Full exit at $66 target or if competitive moat evidence deteriorates (Stripe/Apple Pay market share data).

trades.entry_strategy: Limit buy at $248-$252, using any weakness toward lower end of recent consolidation. Do not chase above $260 until SMA50 slope turns positive.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Adobe is an elite franchise — 58.8% ROE, 38.8% operating margins, $9.3B FCF — trading at a forward P/E of 9.5 and PEG of 0.70. This is a generational valuation for a near-monopoly in creative software with deep AI integration (Firefly). The sell-off from $420 to $225 reflects AI disruption fear that is proving overblown as Firefly monetizes and enterprise demand remains firm. Revenue growth of 12% is durable. Technical: At only 13% of its 52w range, this is deep in Stage 1 basing territory. Price is right at the SMA50 (within 0.1%), and while the SMA50 slope is still -5.4% — a caution — at this valuation the asymmetry strongly favors waiting for one more week of stabilization before the slope inevitably turns. Buying near the 52w low base with a 2x ATR stop gives exceptional RR.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if SMA50 slope fails to improve and price drops through $231 (stop). Reassess if quarterly revenue growth decelerates below 8%. Take partial profits at $300 (psychological resistance). Full target $340 = rough mean-reversion toward 200-day SMA. Exit in full if AI disruption evidence accelerates beyond what current margins can absorb.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit buy at $455-$462 on any minor weakness. Current price is near SMA50 support; acceptable entry zone. Avoid if broad market sells off sharply — wait for stabilization.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: AppLovin is arguably the highest-quality business in this screened universe by operating metrics — 76.9% operating margins, 212.9% ROE, 65.9% revenue growth, all while generating $2.7B FCF. The AI-driven AXON advertising engine is compounding market share in mobile gaming and expanding into e-commerce. Fwd P/E of 22.6 is reasonable for this growth trajectory; PEG of 1.25 makes it cheap on a growth-adjusted basis. Technical: Price has consolidated from the $733 peak down to $301 and has now recovered to $460 — at 37% of 52w range, still in the lower-middle basing zone. SMA50 slope is -1.4%, essentially flat. The basing structure after a 60% correction from highs, combined with fundamentals of this quality, offers an asymmetric setup if the trend confirms continuation. ATR of 5.1% warrants a wider stop but position is sized accordingly.
trades.exit_plan: Stop at $413 (2x ATR below entry). Exit if quarterly revenue growth decelerates meaningfully below 40% or AXON ROAS metrics deteriorate. Partial profit at $550; hold remainder toward $620. Time stop: 120 days if no material progress. Monitor for any regulatory action on mobile advertising or Apple/Google policy changes that threaten the ad-tech model.
